# Plan: Unattended SPE loop, round 5 onward

## What this plan covers

You asked me to run SPE rounds on my own overnight. This plan covers round 5 and every round after it until a stop or halt rule fires. Each round runs Specify, Predict, Evaluate, and Learn in that order. I commit locally after each step. I never push, deploy, or send anything.

I wrote this plan without reading the repo. Before round 5 starts, I will read `spe/README.md`, the round 4 rows in `spe/prediction-log.md`, the "Proposed for round 5" table in `spe/spec/spec.md`, and `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml`. If anything there conflicts with this plan, the repo files win and I log the conflict in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`.

## Limits for the night

These are defaults. I log each one in `spe/spec/disagreements.md` so you can change them in the morning.

| Limit | Default | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Round cap | 4 rounds at most (r05 to r08) | You said "as many as make sense." Four rounds is enough for the 3-round match rule to fire, and few enough for you to review in one sitting. |
| Time cutoff | No new round starts after 05:00 local. A running Workflow may finish. | You see a closed round in the morning, not a half-run one. |
| Spend per round | 1.25 times the measured paid spend of r04 | r04 is the only real cost figure I have. The extra 25% covers split-cell retries. |
| Spend for the night | 3 times the measured paid spend of r04 | This stops 4 rounds from costing more than about 3 rounds of r04. |
| Trials over a cap | Skipped and logged, never run | The way requires this. |

## Stop rules

- I stop when predictions match results for 3 rounds in a row. Before r05, I count how many of r02 to r04 already matched. If r03 and r04 both matched, a match in r05 ends the loop.
- If every configuration passes every check, I do not run the same round again. The next round gets harder tasks or stricter graders. I make that change once as a logged default. If the harder version would change one of your stated requirements, I halt instead.
- I stop when the round cap, time cutoff, or nightly spend cap is reached.

## Halt rules

I halt, write the report, and do nothing more when any of these happen:

- A spend cap would be crossed.
- A trial read a grader, an answer key, or a prediction file. I void the trial first, then halt.
- A grader is broken. That means the selftest fails, the control regrade of the last round does not reproduce its numbers, or a grader bug turns up after a run.
- A decision only you can make comes up. Examples are changing a requirement you wrote, dropping a configuration you asked for, or raising a cap.
- A gate fails twice in a row after a fix attempt.

## Each round, step by step

### 1. Specify

- For r05, I save your overnight message verbatim as `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md`. Later rounds have no new words from you, so their transcripts state that and name r05 as the source.
- I add one requirement table for the round to `spe/spec/spec.md`. Each row has an ID, Requirement, Source, and Test. Each source is your words, a logged default, or a failure ID such as "r04 F3".
- I go through each row of the last round's "Proposed for round N" table. I adopt or reject each one and give a reason. Each choice goes into `spe/spec/disagreements.md` as a default, because you are not here to approve it.
- Commit: `SPE rNN specify`.

### 2. Predict

- I start from `spe/predictions/r(NN-1)-draft.yaml`. Every number begins as "same as last round." I move a number only when I can state the reason in one line.
- The table has one row per metric and one column per configuration. Every cell holds a number. Each row names its grader check and has a one-line Why.
- Each configuration changes one thing from the baseline.
- I copy the plan to `spe/plans/rNN.md`.
- I write `spe/predictions/rNN.yaml`. Its first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds the round, date, author, configs, numbers, a Why per number, and `same_as_last_round`.
- The author field says who approved the round. For r05 it reads "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode (overnight loop plan)." For r06 and later it reads "Claude, autonomous overnight round, not reviewed by the user."
- Commit: `SPE rNN predict: <one-line summary>`. I make this commit before any harness work.
- I never edit a saved prediction after a trial runs.

### 3. Evaluate

- I write `spe/evals/harness/rNN-workflow.js`. One `ROUND` constant holds the round number. No prompt text has a round number typed by hand.
- Trials return results that match a schema. Code checks run first. Judges grade only what code cannot check.
- Trials cannot reach graders, answer keys, or prediction files. After the run, I scan every transcript for reads of those paths.
- Every paid resource has a cap inside the script. Trials that would cross a cap are skipped and logged.
- Before launch I run 3 gates in this order:
  1. The grader selftest. The oracle answer must pass. An empty answer and a wrong answer must fail.
  2. A regrade of the last round as a control. It must reproduce the logged numbers.
  3. A dry run on 2 or 3 cells.
- Commit: `SPE rNN evaluate (harness)`.
- I launch one Workflow. A Workflow returns at launch, so I wait for its completion notice. I do not start the next round while one is running.
- Split cells get extra trials up to the cap. The run ends with failure analysis and a completeness critic.
- Commit: `SPE rNN evaluate (results): <headline>`.

### 4. Learn

- In `spe/prediction-log.md` I add rows with Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under the table, "Which Why broke" quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. If "same as last round" beat my moved numbers, I say so plainly.
- In `spe/failures.md` I add each new failure type. Each entry has the name, kind, round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. A grader bug found after the run counts as a failure. I keep the original and regraded numbers side by side.
- I add a "Proposed for round N+1" table to the spec. I write `spe/predictions/rNN-draft.yaml` marked `status: draft`.
- I update `spe/README.md`.
- Commit: `SPE rNN learn: <one-line summary>`. Tag `spe-rNN` locally.
- I then check the stop and halt rules before starting the next round.

## What I will not do tonight

- I will not push, open PRs, deploy, or send any message or notification.
- I will not change graders during a round. A grader fix goes into the next round's spec as a failure-sourced row.
- I will not edit files outside `spe/` except where a harness needs it. I will not change settings, permissions, or CLAUDE.md.
- I will not rewrite git history, force anything, or delete earlier rounds' files.
- Commit messages will not mention Claude or carry attribution lines, per your CLAUDE.md.

## Morning report

When the loop ends, I leave one report in chat. It has:

- Each round's headline result, one line per round.
- The prediction accuracy trend across r02 to the last round, with the share of cells that matched in each round.
- Measured spend per round and for the night, against the caps.
- Any halt, its cause, and the file that shows it.
- Every default I logged that needs your yes or no.
- The local commits and tags made. Nothing will be pushed.
